acquisition method: The mass spectrometer was operated in the data-dependent mode.
alkylation reagent: replaced with 100 μl 100 mm iodoacetamide (IAM)/25 mm ABC
alkylation concentration: replaced with 100 μl 100 mm iodoacetamide (IAM)/25 mm ABC
cleavage agent: The dried sample was digested with trypsin prepared in 25 mm ABC at 37 °C overnight
collision energy: Fragmentation was performed with normalized collision energy of 35% and an activation time of 0.1 ms.
enrichment method: followed by isopycnic sucrose-gradient ultracentrifugation to separate the inner membrane from the outer membrane.
fragmentation method: The 15 most intense ions were sequentially isolated for higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) MS/MS fragmentation
instrument: connected to the Orbitrap Elite hybrid mass spectrometer (Thermo Electron, Bremen, Germany)
ionization type: NanoLC-nanoESI-MS/MS analysis was performed on a nanoAcquity system
labeling: The iTRAQ method allowed for multiplexing of different samples in the same run by MS analysis
mass analyzer: The 15 most intense ions were sequentially isolated for higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) MS/MS fragmentation and detection in the Orbitrap
precursor tolerance: precursor mass tolerance window as 10 ppm
ptm: dynamic carbamidomethylation on cysteine; dynamic oxidation on methionine; dynamic N-terminal; cysteine iTRAQ labeling

Mascot (v 1.4; Matrix Science, MA, USA) was used for protein identification with the following settings: precursor mass tolerance window as 10 ppm, fragment tolerance window as 50 mmu, dynamic carbamidomethylation on cysteine, dynamic oxidation on methionine, dynamic N-terminal, and cysteine iTRAQ labeling.
reduction reagent: incubated in 100 μl 50 mm dithioerythritol/25 mm ABC in the dark for 1 h at 37 °C
reduction concentration: incubated in 100 μl 50 mm dithioerythritol/25 mm ABC in the dark for 1 h at 37 °C
